name: Tramadol
summary: A weak mu-opioid agonist with additional SNRI-like effects on norepinephrine and serotonin reuptake, used for moderate pain but with genuine opioid risks and a seizure risk.
mechanism: Weak mu-opioid receptor agonist plus inhibition of norepinephrine and serotonin reuptake; the CYP2D6-derived M1 metabolite (O-desmethyltramadol) is a more potent mu agonist.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic (CYP2D6 to active M1 metabolite; CYP3A4 to inactive metabolites)

dosing.adult: 50–100 mg PO q4–6h PRN; start low (50 mg) in opioid-naive patients
dosing.renalAdjustment: Reduce dose or extend interval in renal impairment

safety.pregnancy: Avoid chronic use — neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome and possible respiratory depression at delivery
warnings: Black box: addiction, abuse, and misuse — risk of opioid use disorder
Black box: life-threatening respiratory depression — especially in opioid-naive or elderly patients and with CNS depressants
Black box: accidental ingestion (especially by children) can be fatal
Black box: neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome with prolonged use during pregnancy
CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolizers can rapidly generate M1 and suffer fatal respiratory depression
Lowers the seizure threshold; serotonin syndrome risk with SSRIs/SNRIs/TCAs
monitoring: Respiratory status, especially in opioid-naive or elderly patients
Pain control and signs of misuse
safety.overdose: Respiratory depression, seizures, serotonin syndrome, coma; naloxone partially reverses respiratory depression but not the seizures

indications: Moderate to moderately severe acute pain
Chronic pain (where conventional opioids are undesirable)
clinicalPearls: Analgesia depends on CYP2D6-mediated conversion to M1 — poor metabolizers get little effect, ultrarapid metabolizers risk opioid toxicity
Lowers the seizure threshold — caution in epilepsy and with SSRIs, SNRIs, or TCAs
good: Moderate pain when a conventional opioid is undesirable — but it is still an opioid with real risks.
bad: Seizure-prone patients, serotonergic polypharmacy, CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolizers, or anyone needing predictable analgesia.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard neurology/pharmacology references. Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
